_doc: THE BADGE COINS (Palle, 2026-11-17: 'let the badges be the edge and the artifact of the world and bake them real coins in the world we can pick up. They will change the player and be collected in the badges collation ... connected to the walking path so we know a possible order ... a number and the small text with a symbol like the current badges ... in trans_pre instead of picking count we can pick, translate, rotate and scale. Basic grammar, complex grammar, paradoxes and edges.'). AUTHORED: which coins there are, what each says and gives, and where on the walk it stands. A coin stands either in place of an existing work on its floor ('replaces': a rooms.json artifact id; that work is then not stood) or at a stop of the artifact timeline's walk ('stop': a stop id in commons/data/artifact_timeline_walk.json; the coin hovers over the stop's stand, where the walker arrives). Its NUMBER is derived, never typed: the order of the coins along the walk through the tower (floor by floor downward, then the walk's own order on the floor). tools/badge_coins.ts derives commons/data/badges/path.json (numbers, places, the two faces as SVG built like the research stickers); the game reads only path.json. A coin with 'gives' hands the player a verb when it is collected; until then the verb is missing (Palle, 2026-11-17: locked until collected, acting on the things you place). SEEDED (tools/badge_coins.ts --seed, 2026-11-17; the seed only ADDS a coin whose id is missing and never changes one, so a seeded coin edited or moved by hand stays as it is). GRAMMAR: one coin per spine sequence of commons/modular/grammar.json spine, its root card (commons/modular/terms.json terms[root].card), on the sequence's FIRST tower floor (a floor's sequence is commons/void/spine.json floors[].sequence, read by the floor's MAP, not its index), at the walk's first stop; transformation is skipped (Trans_Pre's four coins are its coins), and so is a sequence whose root is null. Its name is the op word, or the card's own name (the formula's left side, else the term's label) when an earlier coin already carries that op word; its text is the op's adds; its symbol is the op. FAMILY RULE (badge-coins.ts grammarFamily): an op of kind rule, relation, decision, chance or measure is COMPLEX, and so are the combining ops of kind form - assemblage, boolean, field (several parts, or a value everywhere, made one); every other op (form, body, name, number, time: one form turned into the next) is BASIC. PARADOX: one coin per hall that is a tower floor, the hall's FIRST paradox in commons/data/stickers/readings.json order, at the walk's middle stop (of an even walk, the earlier of the two); its name is its first half, whole when that is at most 30 letters, else cut at a word; the second half is its text; its front is the sticker paradox_<reading>. EDGE: every edge reading, named by its kind (EDGE_KINDS), at the last stop of its hall's floor; an edge read outside a hall (the book's log, the misfit ledger) stands where its quote points: at a work it names (a snake_case artifact token standing on a tower floor: at that work's stop), else beside the first coin of a grammar op it names in backticks, else at the bottom of the tower (the last spine floor with a walk), where the walk ends. Two coins never share a stop: a taken stop passes to the next free one along the walk (round to its start), and the seed says so.

basic.title: Basic grammar
basic.note: the acts that turn one form into the next: commons/modular/grammar.json, an operation of one form (genesis, distance, extension, hand, transform ...)

complex.title: Complex grammar
complex.note: acts that combine acts: rule, recursion, rewriting, relation, decision, assemblage (grammar.json)

paradox.title: Paradoxes
paradox.note: two things a hall's text holds true at once (commons/data/stickers/readings.json, kind paradox)

edge.title: Edges
edge.note: where the research says, in its own words, that it stops (readings.json, kind edge)

pick.title: Pick
pick.does: lift a thing you placed and set it down somewhere else

translate.title: Translate
translate.does: move a thing you placed a little: push it away or pull it nearer
translate.vr: while lifting it, push the right stick forward or back

rotate.title: Rotate
rotate.does: turn what you place, and a thing you lift

scale.title: Scale
scale.does: make a thing you placed bigger or smaller
scale.vr: while lifting it, push the right stick left or right
